title: Draw-on lines
summary: Make a line draw itself on with Trim Paths, keying its End, then make it boil with Wiggle Path.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text: Shape operators change a drawn shape each frame. Trim Paths draws only part of a line: animate it and the line draws itself on, like a signature or a route on a map.

steps.title: Select the line
steps.text: Press V and click the blue line. It is a drawing object, so one click picks it whole.

steps.title: Open the Behaviors panel
steps.text: Choose Window > Behaviors if it is not showing. It lists what is on the selection and the settings of each.

steps.title: Add Trim Paths
steps.text: With a shape selected the button reads Add Operator. Click it and choose Trim Paths.

steps.title: Key the End at 0
steps.text:
The playhead is on frame 1. Set End (percent) to 0: the line disappears. Then click the diamond beside it to key it on this frame.

A keyed setting changes over time: Phoenix goes smoothly from each key to the next.

steps.title: End at 100
steps.text: Set End (percent) to 100. Since the setting is keyed, this makes a second key here.

steps.title: Play it
steps.text: Press Enter, or click the play button in the timeline header. The line draws itself on from left to right.

steps.title: Make it boil
steps.text: Click Add Operator and choose Wiggle Path, then tick Change on whole frames only. The line shakes a little each frame, like hand-drawn line work.

steps.title: Well done
steps.text:
You keyed Trim Paths to draw a line on and made it boil. Key Start after it to draw it off again, or use Offset to send a short dash along the line.

Bake turns operators into drawing objects, a frame each, when you need plain frames.
